seo_title: Rooftop Solar Leads in Noida: Filters for Homes vs Societies
description: Rooftop solar leads in Noida: lead form questions and filters that separate kothi owners, RWA committees and flat owners, so your team books more site surveys.
headline: Rooftop solar leads in Noida: how to filter society enquiries from independent house buyers
card_text: Lead filters for Noida installers: the form questions, DISCOM checks and routing rules that separate kothi owners and RWA committees from flat owners who can't install.
intro:
Rooftop solar leads in Noida come with a problem most other NCR cities don't have to the same degree. A large share of the people who click a solar ad here live in high-rise societies along the Expressway, in Noida Extension or in the newer sectors, and most of them can't put panels on the roof by themselves. Meanwhile the kothi and independent house owners in the older plotted sectors, who can say yes on the spot, are a smaller group mixed into the same lead list.

If your form and your first call treat these people the same way, your team spends its day calling flat owners who will never buy and leaves real buyers waiting. This guide gives Noida installers and EPCs a set of lead quality filters: the form questions, the checks on the first call and the routing rules that send a kothi owner to a site survey and an interested flat owner towards their RWA. For the wider picture of who buys solar in the city, see our guide on solar marketing in Noida; this one is only about the leads.

sections.h2: Why Noida solar leads need two pipelines, not one
sections.html:
Almost every rooftop solar enquiry in Noida falls into one of four groups. Only two of them can buy from you this month.

Who is enquiringCan they decide?What to do with the lead
Owner of a kothi, independent house or plot in a plotted sectorYes, usually with familyScore it and book a site survey
RWA or AOA office-bearer, or the society's facility managerPartly: the committee decides, often after a general body meetingMove it to a separate society pipeline with a proposal and meeting
Flat owner in a societyNo, not for the shared roofAsk for an introduction to the committee; don't send a surveyor
Tenant, student or job seekerNoClose politely

A campaign can look cheap because it pulls hundreds of flat owners and still produce almost no surveys. Split the pipelines in your CRM from day one and measure each on its own numbers: surveys for houses, committee meetings for societies.

sections.h2: Lead form questions that filter rooftop solar leads in Noida
sections.html:
On Meta lead forms, click-to-WhatsApp chats and website forms, three or four multiple-choice questions do most of the filtering.

  1. What type of property is it? Kothi or independent house / builder floor / flat in a society / shop, office or factory. This one answer decides which pipeline the lead goes into.
  2. Do you own the property? Yes / No, I rent. Renters usually can't decide on a rooftop system, so this saves a call.
  3. Which sector or area? A short list of the sectors your team actually serves, plus "Greater Noida", "Noida Extension" and "Other".
  4. What is your average monthly electricity bill? Give ranges. A small bill points to a small system, which may not suit your pricing.
  5. For society enquiries only: Are you on the RWA or AOA committee? Yes / No, but I can introduce you / No.

Expect fewer leads at a higher cost per lead; that's the point. Our Facebook ads guide for solar installers shows how to set up these questions in a Meta lead form.

sections.h2: Filters for independent house and kothi leads
sections.html:
Kothi and independent house owners in the older plotted sectors are the leads that turn into installs fastest. Before you book a survey, check these on the first call or chat:

  • Roof rights. In a single-owner kothi, there is no question. In a builder floor, the roof may belong to the top-floor owner or be shared. Ask who owns the roof and whether the other owners agree. A shared roof can mean a builder or co-owner NOC later, so find out now.
  • Shade and free area. Ask for two or three roof photos on WhatsApp. Tanks, a mumty and nearby buildings cut usable area.
  • Sanctioned load. A residential system generally can't be bigger than the connection's sanctioned load. Ask for a recent bill, check the load, and tell the customer early if a load increase is needed.
  • Timeline and payment. Ask when they want to install and whether they plan to pay from their own funds or a loan. A loan buyer needs documents ready before the quote, not after.

A lead that clears all four is worth a survey within a day or two.

sections.h2: Filters for housing society and RWA leads
sections.html:
Society solar is a real opportunity in Noida. In October 2026, district officials in Gautam Budh Nagar were reported to be asking RWAs and AOAs to publicise PM Surya Ghar among residents. But a society lead is a committee sale, and you need different questions to tell a live one from a dead end:

CheckWhy it matters
Is the person on the committee, or can they introduce you to it?An enthusiastic resident without access to the committee rarely moves a proposal forward.
Has the builder handed over the society?If the builder still runs maintenance, or the committee is ad hoc, you may not know who can sign.
Roughly what is the common-area electricity bill?Lifts, pumps, lighting and the DG set drive the savings case. The treasurer or facility manager usually knows the figure.
How much free roof area do the towers have?Tank rooms and lift machine rooms take space on tower roofs. An honest estimate early avoids a proposal that can't be built.
When is the next committee or general body meeting?This becomes your next step and your target date.

A society lead that passes three or more of these checks deserves a proposal and a meeting slot. One that passes none can sit in a monthly nurture list.

sections.h2: Use the electricity bill to check DISCOM, load and subsidy facts
sections.html:
Asking for a recent bill early is the most useful filter in Noida. It settles three questions at once:

  • Which DISCOM. Most of Noida is served by PVVNL, the state-owned DISCOM, and most of Greater Noida by NPCL, a private company. Net-metering applications and inspections go through whichever DISCOM is on the bill, and the steps and timelines differ, so don't explain the process until you've seen it.
  • Who is the consumer. The PM Surya Ghar application is made against the electricity connection. A bill in a landlord's or builder's name changes who you're selling to.
  • Sanctioned load and usage. These tell you the system size the customer can actually install.

When the subsidy comes up, keep it accurate. Under PM Surya Ghar, eligible homes can get central financial assistance of up to ₹78,000 for a system of 3 kW or more, and RWAs and group housing societies get support for common facilities at a separate per-kW rate. Uttar Pradesh has also offered a state top-up for residential rooftop solar, but state amounts and budgets change. Check pmsuryaghar.gov.in and UPNEDA for the current position before you put a number in an ad or a quote, and never call it "free solar". Our guide to PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads has wording that stays true when the scheme changes.

sections.h2: Routing every lead in the first 48 hours
sections.html:
Filters only help if each type of lead gets a clear next step. A simple routing rule your team can follow:

Lead typeFirst contactNext step
Kothi or house owner, in your sectors, bill and photos sharedCall within minutes; WhatsApp if no answerSite survey booked on the call
Kothi owner, details missingCall, then WhatsApp asking for the bill and roof photosSurvey once details arrive; follow up after 2 and 5 days
RWA or AOA office-bearerCall from a senior person, not a junior callerOne-page summary for the committee and a meeting date
Flat owner, interestedWhatsApp messageA short note they can forward to their RWA, and a request for an introduction
Tenant or outside your areaWhatsApp messageClose, or pass to a partner if you have one

Don't ignore the flat owner route: one resident who forwards your note to the committee can open a society project worth far more than a single house.

sections.h2: Check your lead sources every week
sections.html:
Look at the split of leads by type and by source once a week. Some signs that a source is sending the wrong people:

  • More than half its leads are flat owners or tenants. Tighten targeting to plotted sectors and change the creative to show a full kothi rooftop rather than a tower.
  • Many leads list sectors you don't serve. Narrow the location targeting by pincode or radius.
  • Society leads never reach a meeting. Your contacts are probably residents, not committee members, so change who the ad speaks to.

For reference, our rooftop solar campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well, and solar clients at scale typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week. Your results will depend on your sectors, offer and follow-up speed, and no one can promise them in advance. As a solar marketing agency working with 30+ solar EPCs and manufacturers, we start with a 90-day sprint and then move to a flexible arrangement. You can see examples in our solar portfolio, and our guide on rooftop solar leads in Gurgaon shows a lead scoring sheet you can adapt for Noida.

faqs: How do I get rooftop solar leads in Noida?

Most Noida installers use a mix of Meta lead ads, Google Search ads, a well-maintained Google Business Profile, click-to-WhatsApp ads and referrals. Whatever the channel, add questions on property type, ownership, sector and monthly bill so you can tell house owners from flat owners before you call.
Can a flat owner in a Noida society get rooftop solar under PM Surya Ghar?

Not usually on their own, because the tower roof is common property. Societies normally install solar for common areas through the RWA or AOA. Treat interested flat owners as a route to their committee rather than as a direct sale.
Which DISCOM handles rooftop solar in Noida and Greater Noida?
Most of Noida is served by PVVNL and most of Greater Noida by NPCL. The application and inspection go through the DISCOM named on the customer's bill, so check the bill before explaining the process.
What questions should a solar lead form ask in Noida?

Ask the property type (kothi, builder floor, flat or commercial), whether they own it, which sector it is in and their average monthly bill. For society enquiries, also ask whether they are on the RWA or AOA committee.
